_meta.purpose: Sourced religious-vocabulary catalog for the 11 prayer/time names and 5 explanation strings. Companion report: R6-PRAYER-NAME-CATALOG.md; the ten T-410 closures (pt fresh, ha and uz from live media, the loans) are recorded per plan doc T-410; the ten T-419 closures (the ps portal-loan swap, the az and ta Suhoor swaps, the census confirmations and the loans) are recorded per plan doc T-419.

Fajr.note: Bosnian vaktija prints Zora (dawn) for the Fajr row on vaktija.ba; al-azan prints Sabah; Bosnian Islamic usage says Sabah-namaz. Both attested. Zora is the dawn instant; Sabah is the prayer's name.

Sunrise.note: vaktija.ba prints Izlazak sunca; al-azan prints the short Izlazak. Standard Bosnian, astronomical register; the vaktija's full form ships as the sourced label.

Dhuhr.note: Both sources agree: Podne.

Asr.note: Both agree. Bosnian keeps the Turkish loan İkindi as Ikindija.

Magrib.note: Both agree. Akšam (with š) from Turkish Akşam.

Isha.note: Both agree. From Turkish Yatsı via Balkan phonology.

Midnight.note: al-azan prints Ponoć, and vaktija.semerkand.ba's own prose uses ponoć for midnight in the prayer-time context (Hidžretski dan počinje akšamom, a ne u ponoć), the independent Bosnian attestation the census ordered (plan T-419 decision 11). Standard Bosnian.

Last Third.note: Loan per the naming rule: the phrase Bosnian Islamic texts print (the note's record), label-shaped at 19 chars; no vaktija row exists.

Suhoor.note: Loan per the naming rule: the sehur of the recorded sehur/iftar pair, the tr Sahur's Bosnian twin with the h kept; no vaktija row prints the meal.

Duha.note: Loan per the naming rule: the Arabic loan Bosnian texts circle (the note's record; sabahski podne is the rival description); no Bosnian source prints the row.

Istijaba.note: Loan per the naming rule: istijaba in Bosnian's transliteration, dž for the Arabic j as in džamija and džuma; no Bosnian source prints the row.

Halfway between Magrib and Fajr.note: Derived from the sourced Akšam and Sabah with standard Bosnian syntax (sredina između X i Y).

Fajr.note: KMSH prints Imsaku for the dawn row, with الفجر as its Arabic gloss. Same İmsak convention as Turkish. The prayer's name in Albanian religious prose is Sabahu (KMSH's own site uses Sabah-namaz in Albanian too); the table label is Imsaku, kept per plan T-419 decision 13 as the tr İmsak precedent applied, not a new exception, with the same convention note in the catalog's help text.

Sunrise.note: KMSH prints Lindja (rising), short for Lindja e Diellit, with الشروق as its Arabic gloss. takvimi.net prints Lindja e Diellit in full.

Dhuhr.note: KMSH prints Yleja for noon (from Turkish Öğle). Albanian Islamic prose also says Dreka (takvimi.net prints Dreka). Both current: Yleja on KMSH, Dreka on takvimi.net.

Asr.note: KMSH and takvimi.net both print Ikindia. From Turkish İkindi.

Magrib.note: Both print Akshami. From Turkish Akşam.

Isha.note: Both print Jacia. From Turkish Yatsı via Balkan phonology.

Midnight.note: Loan per the naming rule: the ordinary Albanian word, attested in the KMSH-style posts the note records (nga mesnata); KMSH prints no midnight row.

Last Third.note: Loan per the naming rule: the last-third fraction in Albanian's own ordinal syntax, night dropped for the label budget as the owner's D81 ruling did for ms; no Albanian authority prints the row.

Suhoor.note: Loan per the naming rule: the meal word has no Albanian row (the recorded imsaku/iftari pair names the fast's bounds), so the Ottoman-route Sahur lands, the same channel as Yleja, Ikindia, Akshami and Jacia. Imsaku stays the deadline on the Fajr row.

Duha.note: Loan per the naming rule: the Arabic loan in Albanian's Latin script; no Albanian source prints the row.

Istijaba.note: Loan per the naming rule: istijaba in Albanian's transliteration, xh for the Arabic j as in xhami (mosque); no Albanian source prints the row.

Fajr.note: Thai Islamic media print ซุบฮิ (muslimthaipost) or ศุบฮิ (whitechannel). Both are the Thai script renderings of Subhi. muslimthaipost also prints อิมซาก as a separate earlier row, confirming the Imsak/Subuh split in Thai.

Sunrise.note: muslimthaipost prints ตะวันขึ้น (plain Thai for sunrise). whitechannel prints ชุรูก (the Arabic loan Suruq). Two conventions: Thai-native at muslimthaipost, Arabic loan at whitechannel.

Dhuhr.note: Both sources print ซุฮฺริ/ซุฮ์รี variants. Note the ฮฺ (with nikhahit) vs ฮ์ (with thanthakhat) punctuation variance between sources.

Asr.note: Both print อัศริ (Asri).

Magrib.note: Both print มัฆริบ (Maghrib, with the ฆ for gh).

Isha.note: whitechannel prints อีชาอฺ; muslimthaipost prints อิชา. The final อฺ (alif with nikhahit) is the hamza marker.

Midnight.note: No Thai table row found. Thai says เที่ยงคืน. Needs a speaker.

Last Third.note: No Thai source found. Thai Islamic audio uses Tahajjud (ตะฮัจญุด). Needs a speaker.

Suhoor.note: Thai Ramadan calendars say ซูฮูร or อาหารก่อนถือศีลอด. Needs a speaker.

Duha.note: Thai Islamic preachers teach ละหมาดดุฮา (Duha prayer), attested in sermon titles. Single-source-class evidence.

Sunrise.note: true-time and dateandtime.info both print Nascer do sol; namazvakti agrees. R9 §2's attested pattern: the five transliterated plus the translated Sunrise. dateandtime title-cases do Sol in its header; sentence case is the running-text form.

Dhuhr.note: FAMBRAS, true-time and dateandtime print Dhuhr; namazvakti prints Dhur as a variant. All four tables agree on the shape.

Asr.note: All four tables print Asr.

Magrib.note: All four tables print Maghrib, keeping the h (unlike the app's English Magrib spelling, a Latin-script issue only).

Isha.note: true-time, dateandtime and namazvakti print Isha; FAMBRAS's prose prints Ishaa with the doubled a. Isha matches the app's other Latin catalogs.

Midnight.note: No pt table prints the row. luzdoislam's five-prayers article reads o horário para 'Isha dura até à meia-noite, and Isha's deadline is the Islamic midnight, so the word lands in an Islamic-time context. R9 §2 flagged it for a speaker pass; plain form per the shortest-context-correct rule (the D81 precedent).

Last Third.note: R9 §2's candidate for the speaker pass, ordinary Portuguese (terço = third); no pt table or authority text found printing the row.

Suhoor.note: Loan per the naming rule: the Arabic loan Portuguese-language Ramadan calendars use for the meal-time. No pt authority table found; R9 §2 flagged Suhoor for the speaker pass.

Duha.note: Loan per the naming rule: the transliteration, the form pt Muslim texts circle (oração do Duha). No pt source prints the row.

Istijaba.note: Loan per the naming rule: the Arabic name transliterated, the so precedent. No pt source names the hour.
